question:
At postpartum physical examination, a newborn is found to have male external genitalia. Scrotal examination shows a single palpable testicle in the right hemiscrotum. Ultrasound of the abdomen and pelvis shows an undescended left testis, seminal vesicles, uterus, and fallopian tubes. Chromosomal analysis shows a 46, XY karyotype. Which of the following sets of changes is most likely to be found in this newborn?
 $$$ SRY-gene activity %%% Müllerian inhibitory factor (MIF) %%% Testosterone %%% Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) $$$?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: SRY-gene activity -> Testosterone -> Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) -> Normal normal ↑ ↑ -> 80%
CHAIN: Müllerian inhibitory factor (MIF) -> Inhibition of Müllerian duct development -> Absence of uterus and fallopian tubes -> ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ -> 90%
enhanced_information: In this newborn with male external genitalia, a single palpable testicle in the right hemiscrotum, undescended left testis, seminal vesicles, uterus, and fallopian tubes, and a 46, XY karyotype, the most likely set of changes involves a decrease in SRY-gene activity leading to a decrease in testosterone, dihydrotestosterone (DHT), Müllerian inhibitory factor (MIF), resulting in a decrease in all parameters (↓ ↓ ↓ ↓). The interaction between testosterone and stanolone supports the downstream effects on DHT levels.
